name: Memory Cartography
definition: A craft in which an accurate survey transfers one autobiographical memory from its source into the finished map, so the map becomes both a record of place and an archive of what someone paid to know it.
motivating_story_use: Makes accurate knowledge carry an intimate, distributable cost that the Guild can hoard, trade, or conceal.
why_existing_concepts_insufficient: Setup and Payoff describe narrative structure, and Conflict describes opposition, but neither expresses a reusable object or practice whose truth is purchased with autobiographical loss and whose ownership can become political.
proposed_relations: Memory Cartography specializes Setup by making the price of knowledge concrete before its payoff.
Memory Cartography creates tension with Theme when memory is treated as identity rather than information.
Memory Cartography gives Conflict an owned instrument: whoever controls the maps controls which memories remain public.
compatibility_concerns: Do not imply that every setting permits supernatural memory transfer.
Do not treat the erased memory as simply recoverable; the story's cost depends on irreversibility.
The concept is project-scoped until a separate ontology review accepts a general definition.
